### Is paying for Google ads better than SEO for a small business?

Neither is better for every business. Paid search ads can bring calls within days, and they stop the moment you stop paying. SEO usually takes months to build, but the visibility it earns tends to last after the work slows. One option is to use ads to cover gaps while SEO builds, then lean on whichever brings in customers at the lower cost per job.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-paid-search-better-than-seo/

### What should a good SEO proposal include?

A good SEO proposal says in plain words what work will be done, what will be measured and how you will see it, who does the work, what you will own, what you must provide, and how either side can end the agreement. If a proposal promises rankings, keeps the work vague, or would leave you unable to walk away with your own website and accounts, keep looking.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-an-seo-proposal-include/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### How do you switch marketing agencies without losing your website or leads?

Switch in an order that keeps you in control. First confirm that you own, and can log in to, your domain, website, hosting, analytics, ad accounts and business profiles. Then give notice. Before access ends, collect your content, lead data, phone numbers and reports. Overlap the old and new agency briefly where you can, and change passwords once the handover is done.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-switch-marketing-agencies/

### What is a CRM, and does a small business need one?

A CRM (customer relationship management system) is one shared place that records every customer and inquiry: who they are, how they found you, what was said and what happens next. A small business does not always need dedicated software. A well-kept spreadsheet or shared board often works at first. A CRM earns its place when inquiries start slipping through, follow-ups get missed, or more than one person handles leads.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-crm/

### How should a small business handle inquiries that arrive after hours?

Acknowledge every after-hours inquiry right away with an automatic reply that thanks the person and says exactly when a real reply will come, such as by 9 the next morning. Then keep that promise: make overnight inquiries the first task of the next working day, and set a clear weekend rule so no one waits until Monday without knowing it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-handle-leads-after-hours/

### How do you write a good first reply to a new inquiry?

A good first reply to a new inquiry does four things in a few short sentences: it thanks the person by name, answers the question they actually asked, offers one clear next step, and says when that step will happen. It should read as if a person wrote it for them, not like a template, and it should go out quickly.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-reply-to-a-new-inquiry/

### What should you ask a customer after the work is done?

After the work is done, ask four things: how it went and what could have been better, how they first found you, whether they would be willing to share a review, and whether they know anyone else who needs the same help. Ask every customer, not only the happy ones, offer nothing in return for a review, and record the answers.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-ask-customers-after-the-job/
Sources: https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### Where should a small business start with marketing?

Start with the basics, in order. Know what a customer is worth to you. Make sure every inquiry reaches a person and is recorded with its source. Fix the website basics so visitors can see what you do and how to contact you. Then work on getting found through search, AI answers, referrals and reviews. Finally, check the numbers once a month and adjust.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/where-should-a-small-business-start-with-marketing/

### Do you need a website if you already get customers from social media?

Usually, yes. Social media can bring in customers, but a profile lives on someone else's platform, under their rules, and can be limited or lost without warning. A website is a place you own, that search engines and AI assistants can find and describe, and that gives every customer one clear place to check you out and get in touch. Social alone can work for a while, mostly when referrals already fill the calendar.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-you-need-a-website-if-you-use-social-media/

### Who should own your business's domain name?

The business should own its domain name, registered in the business's name, in a registrar account the business controls, with a login the owner can reach. A web designer, agency or former employee can be given access, but should not be the registrant. When someone else holds the domain, your website and email depend on them renewing it and handing it over when you ask.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-should-own-your-domain-name/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/benefits-2013-09-16-en ; https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/whois-rdds-2023-11-02-en

### Should a service business put prices on its website?

It depends on how predictable your work is. Showing prices tends to screen out people who were never going to buy, and it answers the first question most visitors have. But when every job is different, a single number can mislead or scare off good customers. Many service businesses do well with a middle ground: a starting-from range, a plain list of what changes the price, and an example of a typical job.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-put-prices-on-your-website/

### How do you make a website trustworthy to a new visitor?

Show a new visitor that a real, reachable business is behind the site. Put your phone number, email and service area where they are easy to find. Use photos of your own work and people, share real reviews you have permission to use, explain your prices or process plainly, and keep everything up to date. Small errors such as typos and broken links undo a lot of that work quickly.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-make-a-website-trustworthy/
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/trustworthy-design/

### Does a small business website really need to work well on phones?

Yes. Pew Research Center's Mobile Fact Sheet reports that about nine in ten U.S. adults (91%) own a smartphone. Often, the phone is the first place people look for help. If your website is slow, hard to read or hard to act on from a phone, many visitors will leave before they call. You can test the basics yourself in a few minutes.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/does-your-website-need-to-work-on-phones/
Sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/

### What is Perplexity, and do customers use it to find businesses?

Perplexity describes itself as an AI-powered search engine. You type a question, it searches the web, and it writes an answer in plain language with links to the sources it used. A customer can ask it who to hire for a job, and the answer may name businesses. Because it shows its sources, a business can see which pages shaped what Perplexity said about it, and fix what it controls.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-perplexity/
Sources: https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352155-what-is-perplexity

### How do you get found for a new service you just started offering?

Start by saying it plainly on your website: what the new service is, who it is for and where you offer it. Then tell the customers you already have, because they are the quickest first buyers and the likeliest to refer you. Ask the first customers who use it for an honest review. After that, be patient: it usually takes months, not weeks, for a new service to be found by strangers.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-found-for-a-new-service/

### How much of your marketing should you do yourself?

Do the parts of marketing that depend on you: talking to customers, asking for reviews and referrals, and replying to new inquiries quickly. Hand off work that takes you far longer than a specialist, keeps slipping down the list, or needs skills you do not want to learn. Whatever you hand off, keep ownership of the accounts, so the website, domain and profiles stay yours.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-much-marketing-should-you-do-yourself/

### What is a marketing retainer, and how should one work?

A marketing retainer is an agreement to pay a set monthly fee for an agreed amount of ongoing marketing work, instead of paying by the project or by the hour. A fair retainer spells out what gets done each month, how success is measured, how and when you get a report, how long the term is, how much notice either side must give, and that you own your accounts and the work.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-marketing-retainer/

### How should a seasonal business plan its marketing?

Plan around the calendar, not the month in front of you. Start marketing before the busy season, because customers often look and compare weeks before they book. Stay visible in the off season so you are not starting from nothing next year. Use quiet months to improve the website and ask last season's customers for reviews. Then judge results by comparing each season with the same season last year.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/marketing-for-seasonal-businesses/

### Which source gets the credit when a customer found you several ways?

Record both. First touch is the channel that introduced a person to your business; last touch is the channel they used just before they got in touch. First touch shows what makes new people aware of you, and last touch shows what turns that interest into an inquiry. Keep both on every lead, pick one as your main view for decisions, and apply the same rule every time so the numbers stay comparable.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/which-source-gets-credit-for-a-customer/

### Should a small business have a referral program?

Often, yes, if happy customers already send friends your way. A referral program makes that habit easier to notice, track and thank. Keep it simple: one clear ask at the end of a job, one question to every new inquiry about who sent them, and one thank-you that is the same for everyone and stated in advance. If a referrer mentions a reward in a public post, they should usually say plainly that they get something for referrals.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-have-a-referral-program/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking

### Is email marketing worth it for a small service business?

Usually, yes, when it goes to people who already know you: past customers and people who asked about your services. A short, useful email every month or two keeps your name in mind for the next job and for referrals, and costs little time once it is a habit. It works poorly for reaching strangers. Keep each message honest, easy to unsubscribe from and about one thing.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-email-marketing-worth-it-for-a-service-business/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business

### How do you win back customers who have not come back?

Contact past customers who were happy but have gone quiet, with a short, honest message: it has been a while, you are still here, and here is something useful, such as a reminder that a service is due. Ask whether anything changed or fell short, and listen. Offer only what you really offer, with no invented deadlines or discounts. One message and one follow-up is usually enough; then stop.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-win-back-past-customers/

### How do you set up a simple lead tracker?

Use one shared sheet or board with a row for every inquiry and eight columns: date, name, contact details, what they need, source channel, first reply time, outcome and notes. Follow one rule: every inquiry from every channel goes in the same day it arrives. Then review it once a month to see where work comes from, how fast you answer and which inquiries turn into paid jobs.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-set-up-a-simple-lead-tracker/

### What is a call to action, and what makes a good one?

A call to action is the line or button that tells a visitor what to do next, such as "Call for a quote" or "Book a visit". A good one asks for a single step, uses a plain verb, says what happens after the click, and uses the same wording everywhere it appears. Each page should have one main call to action, repeated where a reader is ready to act.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-call-to-action/

### What is a landing page, and when does a small business need one?

A landing page is a single web page built for one purpose, usually one campaign, ad or flyer. It repeats the offer the visitor responded to, answers the questions that offer raises, and asks for one next step. A small business needs one when it is sending people to a specific offer. For general visitors, a clear homepage and service pages are usually enough.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-landing-page/

### How should you describe your services on your website?

Describe each service the way your customers would ask for it, not in trade terms. Say what is included, who it is for, how the job works from first call to finish, and what happens after someone gets in touch. Add real examples of past jobs. A customer who can picture the work and the next step is usually more likely to call than one reading a list of service names.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-describe-your-services-on-your-website/

### What is website accessibility, and why does it matter for a small business?

Website accessibility means a site is built so people with disabilities can use it, including people who are blind, deaf, or cannot use a mouse. It matters for a small business because a site that shuts people out loses customers, and because U.S. Department of Justice guidance takes the position that the ADA covers businesses open to the public, online too. Owners can run simple checks themselves, such as image descriptions, contrast, captions and keyboard use; they catch common problems but do not show legal compliance.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-your-website-accessible/
Sources: https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-guidance/ ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/fundamentals/accessibility-intro/

### What photos should a service business use on its website?

A service business should use real photos: the owner, the team, the vehicles and real finished jobs. Get permission from anyone who appears, show before-and-after pairs only if they are genuinely the same job, and never present stock photos as your own work. Keep image files small so pages load quickly on phones. Visitors tend to look closely at real people and real work, and skip generic decoration.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-photos-should-a-service-business-website-use/
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/photos-as-web-content/

### Is it too late for a small business to start SEO?

Usually not. Search is more crowded than it was, and AI answers can now settle some questions before anyone clicks, so many of the easy wins of years ago are often gone. But customers still look before they hire, and a late starter can still be found for specific services, in the areas it genuinely serves, and for first-hand answers larger sites cannot write. Start with the basics and expect months, not weeks.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-it-too-late-to-start-seo/
Sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### Should you hire a freelancer or an agency for SEO and marketing?

Either can work. A freelancer often means one skilled person you deal with directly, usually with lower overheads but less cover when they are away. An agency usually brings a wider range of skills and someone to step in, though you may talk to an account manager rather than the person doing the work. Whichever you choose, the questions that matter most are the same: who owns the accounts, and what gets reported.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/freelancer-or-agency-for-seo/

### What is Google Gemini, and do customers use it to find businesses?

Gemini is Google's AI assistant, first launched as Bard in March 2023 and renamed Gemini in February 2024. Google describes it as an interface to a large language model that can draw on outside sources such as Google Search when it writes an answer. About a quarter of U.S. adults say they use it, according to Pew Research Center, so some customers may ask it who to hire.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-google-gemini/
Sources: https://gemini.google/overview/ ; https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/bard-gemini-advanced-app/ ; https://gemini.google/about/ ; https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13695044?hl=en ; https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### How do you tell whether a change to your website worked?

Write down the date of every change, then compare the inquiries that arrived in the weeks after it with the same number of weeks before, and with the same weeks last year if your work is seasonal. Change one thing at a time where you can, give it long enough to show, and judge it by inquiries and customers, not by clicks or visits.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-tell-if-a-website-change-worked/

### How do customers compare service businesses online before they call?

Before they call, customers usually compare a few businesses on what they can see in minutes: how many reviews each has and how recent they are, whether the owner replies, photos of real work, a plain statement of services and area, and how quickly anyone answers. In BrightLocal's 2026 survey of U.S. adults, 47% said they would not use a business with fewer than 20 reviews.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-customers-compare-businesses-online/
Sources: https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/

### How do you spot spam and scam inquiries from your website?

Spam and scam inquiries usually give themselves away. They ignore what you actually offer, carry links you did not ask for, push you to act fast, offer to overpay, or ask for payment by wire transfer, gift card or cryptocurrency. Do not click their links or send business details in reply. Check any claim through a contact you already trust, keep the message out of your lead numbers, and report real scams to the FTC.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-spot-spam-and-scam-inquiries/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business

### What should you do with a lead you cannot serve?

Reply quickly and kindly, even when the answer is no. Thank the person, say plainly why you cannot help, and point them somewhere useful, such as another business you trust. Then record the inquiry with its source, an outcome of lost and the reason. Over time, those reasons can show whether people keep asking for a service you do not offer, or whether some of your marketing is reaching the wrong people.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-do-with-leads-you-cannot-serve/

### Should you call or email a new lead first?

Reply on the channel the person used, unless they asked for a different one. A form or email inquiry gets an email first; a missed call gets a call back. If they left a phone number and the job needs a conversation, a quick call can help, followed by a short email so they have it in writing. Call or text only with the person's consent, and record every attempt you make.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-call-or-email-a-new-lead-first/

### What should you say when a new lead asks for the price first?

Answer honestly and directly. If you can give a typical range, give it, along with what moves the price up or down. If you cannot price the job without details, say so, ask the one or two questions you need and explain why. Never dodge the question, and never invent a discount or a deadline to close the sale. A clear, honest answer usually builds trust, even when the number is not what they hoped.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/when-a-lead-asks-for-the-price-first/

### Should a service business let customers book online?

Often yes, when the visit has a fixed length and needs no quote first, such as a consultation, an estimate visit or a standard appointment. Online booking lets customers pick a time without waiting for a reply. It works poorly for jobs that need questions answered or a price agreed first. If you add it, make sure you own the booking data, every booking is confirmed, nothing double-books and each booking is recorded with its source.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-use-an-online-booking-tool/

### What should you get from a website review?

A website review should give you a plain list of what to keep, what to fix and what to replace, ranked by how much each item is likely to affect inquiries, with a short reason for each. It should check how the site works on a phone, whether a visitor can tell quickly what you do, whether the forms and phone links work, and who owns the domain and logins. A review that only sells a rebuild is a sales pitch.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-you-get-from-a-website-review/

### How long does it take to build or upgrade a small business website?

How long a small business website takes depends less on the building than on how quickly words, photos and decisions arrive. Upgrading a site that already works is often a matter of a few weeks; a new site with many pages can take longer. Projects most often stall while waiting for the owner's content and approvals, so gathering those before work starts is usually the biggest single way to speed things up.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-long-does-it-take-to-build-a-website/

### Does a small business website need a privacy policy?

Often yes, and it is a sensible habit either way. California's online privacy law, CalOPPA, as the state Attorney General describes it, requires commercial websites that collect personally identifiable information, such as a name, email address or phone number, from California consumers to post a privacy policy. If any of your visitors are in California, a contact form can bring you within it. A short, honest policy says what you collect, why, who sees it and how to ask for deletion. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/does-a-small-business-website-need-a-privacy-policy/
Sources: https://www.oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-launches-new-tool-help-consumers-report ; https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/facts/online-privacy/privacy-policy ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/protecting-personal-information-guide-business ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/privacy-security/consumer-privacy

### What should a small business put on its About page?

A small business About page should say who is behind the business, with real names and photos, how long you have done this work, where you work, how a job runs from first call to finish, what you will not do, and how to get in touch. Every line should be true and easy to check. Visitors often read an About page to decide whether a real, reachable person is behind the website.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-be-on-an-about-page/
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/about-us-information-on-websites/

### Does a small business website need HTTPS?

Yes. HTTPS is the secure version of a web address: it keeps what passes between a visitor's browser and your site private and harder to tamper with. It matters most where visitors type in their details, such as a contact form. Google's Chrome Help says that on a site without a private connection, someone may be able to view and change what visitors send, and Chrome can label such sites "Not secure".

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/does-your-website-need-https/
Sources: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95617?hl=en ; https://web.dev/articles/why-https-matters

### Will AI assistants call or contact businesses on a customer's behalf?

Some already do. In July 2025 Google said Search can use AI to call local businesses for pricing and availability on a customer's behalf, for needs from pet grooming to dry cleaning. Google's help pages say its automated calls can also book appointments and check restaurant wait times, and that businesses can opt out. For an owner, it means answering the phone and having clear answers on prices and availability ready.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/will-ai-assistants-contact-businesses-for-customers/
Sources: https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/deep-search-business-calling-google-search/ ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/7690269?hl=en ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/6212928?hl=en

### Are paid directory listings worth it for a small business?

Sometimes, but judge each one by the inquiries it actually sends, not by what the salesperson says. A paid listing usually buys a better spot or a fuller profile on someone else's website. Start with the free version where there is one, record where every inquiry came from, and renew only if paid jobs arrive from it. Be wary of long contracts, promises of a top spot, and any "free" listing that later comes with a bill.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-paid-directory-listings-worth-it/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business

### How much of an owner's time does SEO and GEO work take?

Usually less than owners expect, but never none. Most of the owner's part is knowledge only you have: answering questions about the business, approving what goes live, supplying real photos, asking customers for reviews and reading a short report each month. The first weeks often take more of your time; after that, an hour or two a month is often enough. The work tends to stall fastest when approvals sit waiting.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-much-time-does-seo-take-from-an-owner/

### Should you add keywords or a city to your business name to show up more in search?

Not on your Google Business Profile. Google's guidelines say the name should reflect your business's real-world name, and that adding unnecessary information, such as a service or a location, is not permitted and could get the profile suspended. Renaming the business itself to include a service or a city is a separate business decision, best made for your customers and your brand, not for search.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-put-keywords-in-your-business-name/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177

### Can AI write your website copy?

AI can help with drafts, outlines and tidying your own words, but it should not have the last word. It does not know your prices, your service area, your policies, your past jobs or how you talk to customers, and it can state wrong facts with confidence. Use it to get started, then have a person who knows the business check every fact, claim and promise before anything goes live.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-ai-write-your-website/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content ; https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/08/federal-trade-commission-announces-final-rule-banning-fake-reviews-testimonials

### How do you get referrals from other businesses?

Find a few businesses that serve the same customers as you without competing, such as a painter and a flooring installer, and ask plainly whether sending work both ways would help. Make it easy for them: one short line about what you do and one link to pass on. Send good work back when it fits. Record every referral with the source channel referral and the partner's name, so you can see which partnerships bring jobs.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-referrals-from-other-businesses/

### What is a sales pipeline for a small service business?

A sales pipeline is the set of stages an inquiry moves through after it has been answered: a lead system gets the inquiry in and answered, and the pipeline tracks what happens next. For a small service business, a few plain stages usually cover it: new, contacted, quote or visit booked, quote sent, and an outcome of won, lost or still open. Knowing which stage each lead is in shows where jobs stall, so you can fix that step instead of only chasing more inquiries.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-sales-pipeline/

### How do you write a quote that wins the job?

A quote that tends to win the job reads like an answer to the customer's problem, not a price list. Restate what they need in their own words, say what is included and what is not, give the timing, explain what happens after they say yes, and offer one clear way to accept. Add a date the quote is good until only if there is a real reason for one, and never invent urgency.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-write-a-quote-that-wins-the-job/

### Should a service business offer free estimates?

It depends on your work. Free estimates can bring in more inquiries, especially in trades where customers expect them, but every visit to a poor fit costs time you are not paid for. Two common middle grounds are a short screen of a few questions before any visit, and a paid assessment that is credited to the job if the customer goes ahead. Whatever you choose, say it plainly on your website.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-offer-free-estimates/

### How many inquiries does a small business need to hit its goals?

Work backwards from your goal. Take the number of new jobs you want each month and divide it by the share of inquiries that usually turn into paid work. If you want ten new jobs and you win about one inquiry in four, you need about forty inquiries a month. Then look at where your inquiries come from today and decide which channels can realistically supply the gap.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-many-inquiries-do-you-need/

### How do you choose a domain name for a small business?

Choose a domain name that is short, easy to say out loud and easy to spell, and as close as possible to your real business name. Avoid hyphens, numbers and clever spellings that people will get wrong. Before you register it, check whether the name may conflict with someone else's trademark, then register it in your business's name so the business, not a vendor, controls it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-choose-a-domain-name/
Sources: https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/search/comprehensive-clearance-search-similar-trademarks ; https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/search/federal-trademark-searching

### Should a small business have more than one website?

Usually not. Most small service businesses do better with one website that covers all their services and areas. A second site often splits the work, the updates and the attention customers give you, and it can leave people unsure which one is real. A separate site tends to make sense only for a genuinely separate business or brand, with its own name and its own customers.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-a-small-business-have-more-than-one-website/

### What should a small business look for in website hosting?

Look for hosting with the account in your business's name, regular backups you can actually restore, support you can reach when the site is down, secure connections included, pages that load quickly, and renewal terms written in plain words. It should also be easy to leave with a full copy of your site. The brand matters much less than those basics.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-look-for-in-website-hosting/

### Does a small business need website analytics?

Usually yes, kept simple. Website analytics shows how many people visit, which pages they read and where they came from, which helps you spot pages that are not working. It cannot tell you who became an inquiry or a customer; only your own lead records can. Use analytics as a supporting view, collect only what you need, and say in your privacy notice what you use.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-you-need-website-analytics/

### What should a website say after someone sends an inquiry?

After someone sends an inquiry, the page or message they see should confirm it arrived, say when and how you will reply, explain what happens next, and tell them what to do if the matter is urgent. One useful link to read while they wait is a good addition. Promise only a reply time you can keep every day, and keep what they sent private.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-thank-you-page-say/

### Should you buy leads from sites like Angi or Thumbtack?

It can be worth it, but judge each lead site by the jobs you actually win from it, not by how many leads it sends. Leads on these sites are often shared with other businesses, so a fast, useful first reply matters. Record every lead with its source and outcome, and keep each customer's details in your own lead list, not only inside the site's app.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-buy-leads-from-lead-sites/
Sources: https://intercom.help/angi/en/articles/6221483-opportunities-and-leads-frequently-asked-questions ; https://intercom.help/angi/en/articles/11403440-how-to-request-a-lead-credit ; https://www.thumbtack.com/pro

### What are Google Local Services Ads, and are they worth it?

Google Local Services Ads are ads in Google Search, offered for certain local service categories, where a business pays for leads, such as calls and messages. Every business must pass Google's screening and verification to take part, and in some categories it can then show a Google Verified badge. They can be worth it for a business that answers every lead quickly and judges the ads by booked jobs, not by lead count.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-are-google-local-services-ads/
Sources: https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841 ; https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226575 ; https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7435486

### Should a small business use an answering service or an AI receptionist?

Either can beat voicemail, which many callers may skip. A human answering service usually handles unusual or upset callers better; an AI receptionist answers at once, at any hour, but can say wrong things in your name. Pick the one you can check. Whichever you use, every call should land in your lead list with its source, and calls should be recorded only with the person's consent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/answering-service-or-ai-receptionist/

### Why are my leads not turning into customers?

Usually one stage is leaking, not all of them. Look at your own lead list for the last few months and find where leads stop: wrong-fit leads from one source, slow first replies, no follow-up after the first message, or quotes that never get an answer. Each points to a different fix, and the stage that loses the most leads is the place to start.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-are-leads-not-turning-into-customers/

### How do you keep track of leads that come in through Facebook, Instagram and other messages?

Treat every message that asks about your work as a lead, and copy it into the same lead list as your calls and forms, with social as its source and the platform named. Check each inbox at set times every working day, or use one shared inbox for several platforms. Keep business messaging on accounts the business owns, not on a staff member's personal profile, so the history stays when people leave.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-track-leads-from-social-media-messages/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/business/help/294426838452244

### Who owns the website a designer built for you?

Paying for a website does not, by itself, make you the owner of its design, code and custom images. Under U.S. copyright, the person who creates a work is ordinarily its author and owner, and an outside designer is usually not your employee. A written agreement that assigns the work to your business settles the question. The text and photos you supplied remain yours, and the domain name is a separate matter. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-owns-a-website-a-designer-built/
Sources: https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ30.pdf ; https://www.copyright.gov/help/faq/faq-protect.html

### What should a website design contract include?

A website design contract should pin down the scope (which pages and features), how many revision rounds are included, who supplies the text and photos and by when, who owns the design and files once the work is paid for, which accounts are opened in your business's name, what you receive at handover, and what happens if the project stalls on either side. If ownership is missing from the draft, ask for it before signing.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-website-design-contract-include/
Sources: https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ30.pdf

### How can you tell if your business website has been hacked, and what do you do first?

The usual signs are visible ones: the site sends visitors somewhere else, pages or links appear that you never created, browsers show a security warning before the site loads, customers report strange messages that look like they came from you, or your own login stops working. First steps: take the site offline or have your host do it, change every password, keep the evidence rather than deleting things, and restore a clean backup only after the way in is closed.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-tell-if-your-website-was-hacked/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/data-breach-response-guide-business ; https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/cyber-essentials

### How many pages does a small business website need?

Most small service businesses do well with four to seven pages: a homepage, a page for each main service customers hire you for, an about page and a contact page. A brand-new business with one service in one area can start with a single good page and grow from there. Add a page only when you have something real to put on it; a thin, empty page helps no one, and the count itself wins nothing.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-many-pages-does-a-small-business-website-need/

### How do you get control of your website back when the designer has disappeared?

Start with the domain, because everything else can be rebuilt behind it. Check who is recorded as its holder: if that is your business, recover the registrar account and move the domain to an account you control; if it is the designer, you need their cooperation, the registrar's help, or in the worst case a new domain. Then recover the hosting and platform accounts with proof of identity and billing, and save every page that is still visible before anything disappears.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-your-website-back-from-a-designer/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/transfer-policy-2016-06-01-en ; https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/benefits-2013-09-16-en

### Can you put customer reviews and testimonials on your website?

Yes. Real words from real customers can help a new visitor trust you. The Federal Trade Commission's position is that testimonials should reflect the customer's honest opinion and actual experience, that a connection such as a relative or employee should be made clear, and that unusual results need context about what people generally get, unless the business can show they are typical. A business that posts fake or false testimonials on its own site could be liable. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-put-customer-reviews-on-your-website/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

### Should your business email use your own domain instead of a free address?

Usually, yes. An address at your own domain, the same name as your website, tends to look more established than a free address, and it belongs to the business rather than to one person. When someone leaves, their mailbox can be handed over and customer mail keeps arriving. If you change email providers, the address can stay the same. The main condition is that the business controls the domain and keeps it renewed.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-your-business-email-use-your-own-domain/

### Is a website template good enough for a small business?

For many small service businesses, yes. A good template can look professional, work on a phone and go live quickly. Custom design can be worth it when you need something a template cannot do, or when the look itself is part of what you sell. Either way, the things that usually decide whether a site brings inquiries are clear words, speed on a phone and one obvious next step, not whether the design was custom.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-a-website-template-good-enough/

### How do you spot a fake domain or website renewal notice?

Treat any renewal notice you did not expect as unconfirmed until you check it yourself. Fake ones often come from a company you do not use, warn that your site or email will go dark, and push you to pay through their link or number. Do not pay from the notice or click its links. Type your registrar's address yourself, log in, check the expiry date there, and report fakes at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-spot-a-fake-domain-renewal-notice/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/en/blogs/details/do-you-have-a-domain-name-heres-what-you-need-to-know-30-4-2020-en ; https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/phishing-2013-05-03-en ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business

### What should you do when you get more leads than you can handle?

Keep replying to every lead, and be honest about when you can start. Give a real date, offer a short waitlist to people happy to wait, and put your best-fit jobs first. Pause paid channels before anything else, since they cost money for leads you cannot take, and refer work you cannot do to businesses you trust. Keep recording every lead, so a busy stretch still shows where demand came from.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/more-leads-than-you-can-handle/

### How do you track leads from flyers, yard signs and truck wraps?

Give every printed item its own way back to you, then record it. A flyer, yard sign or truck wrap can carry a short web address or QR code used nowhere else, or its own phone number, so an inquiry that arrives through it can be traced. Ask every new customer how they found you as well. Log these leads under the campaign channel, name the item in the notes, and follow each one to won, lost or still open.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-track-leads-from-flyers-signs-and-vehicles/

### Are Facebook and Instagram lead ads worth it for a service business?

They can be, but judge them by the jobs they bring in, not by how many forms get filled in. Meta's lead ads with an instant form ask people who tap the ad on Facebook or Instagram to fill out a form. Meta says its default form type is designed to bring a larger number of leads. In practice, that can mean more people who were only mildly interested. Record every lead as paid, follow it to won, lost or still open, and compare the jobs won with what you spent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-facebook-lead-ads-worth-it/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1462876307360828 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/252352181957512 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2246428158756947

### Can you use photos you found online on your business website?

Usually not without permission. The U.S. Copyright Office's position is that a work is protected from the moment it is created and fixed in a tangible form, and its FAQ says most works may be assumed protected unless there is clear information to the contrary. Finding a photo online does not make it free to use. Use your own photos, images you hold a license for, or ones whose owner has said yes, ideally in writing. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-use-photos-from-the-internet-on-your-website/
Sources: https://www.copyright.gov/help/faq/faq-fairuse.html ; https://www.copyright.gov/help/faq/faq-general.html ; https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/ ; https://ccb.gov/faq/

### Should your website have a Spanish version?

It is worth it when a real share of your customers prefer Spanish and you can serve them in Spanish, on the phone and on the job as well as on the page. Census Bureau figures show almost one in five people in the United States spoke a language other than English at home in 2019, most often Spanish. Check your own area and inquiries first, and have a fluent person review every page instead of publishing unchecked machine translation.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-your-website-have-a-spanish-version/
Sources: https://www.census.gov/topics/population/language-use.html ; https://www.census.gov/library/publications/2022/acs/acs-50.html ; https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2022/12/languages-we-speak-in-united-states.html

### Should your website show your license number and insurance?

If you hold a license, showing the number usually helps, because a customer can check it with the state quickly. In Florida, contractors registered or certified with the state's Construction Industry Licensing Board must put that number in their offers, bids, contracts and advertisements (as the board's rule defines them), and on vehicles that carry the business name. Mention insurance only if a current policy covers the work, and be ready to show proof. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-your-website-show-your-license-and-insurance/
Sources: https://www.myfloridalicense.com/wl11.asp ; http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0489/Sections/0489.119.html

### What is a Google Business Profile, and does a service business need one?

A Google Business Profile is the free listing Google shows for a business on Search and Maps: name, hours, contact details, photos, reviews and a short description. Google says creating one is free. A business that customers visit, or that travels to customers, can have one, and for most local service businesses it is worth claiming: it is often the first thing a customer sees, and the owner controls part of it but not all of it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://business.google.com/us/business-profile/ ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/2721884 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481

### How do you spot an SEO scam?

Most SEO scams announce themselves: an email or call you did not ask for, a claim that your site is not listed or your listing is about to be lost, pressure to act today, and a promise of a top spot. Google tells site owners to be wary of SEO firms that email out of the blue and says no one can promise a number one ranking. The FTC's advice applies: slow down, check the company, never pay under pressure.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-spot-an-seo-scam/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business ; https://business.google.com/us/business-profile/

### Does paying for Google Ads help you rank higher in the free results?

No. Google says that because it only sells ad space, "no one can buy better placement in organic Search results", and that advertising with Google has no effect on a site's presence in its search results. Ads and the unpaid results are separate systems: running ads buys labeled ad slots for as long as you pay, and stopping them does not lower your free position. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling a myth.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-google-ads-help-your-free-rankings/
Sources: https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Can you pay to show up in ChatGPT or Google's AI answers?

You can pay for an ad beside an AI answer, not for a place in the answer itself. Google shows labeled ads above, below or within AI Overviews, chosen by its normal ad auction, and says advertisers cannot target those placements directly. OpenAI says ads in ChatGPT are separate, clearly labeled and do not influence the answer. The written answer comes from a different system, and a paid recommendation inside it is not a product anyone can sell.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-pay-to-show-up-in-ai-answers/
Sources: https://openai.com/index/our-approach-to-advertising-and-expanding-access/ ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16297775 ; https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Is GEO worth it for a small business?

GEO is worth it when your customers are already asking AI assistants who to hire. Three signs decide it: whether your customers skew under 50, the group that used ChatGPT at about twice the rate of older adults in Pew's 2026 survey; whether your jobs are researched in advance rather than booked in an emergency; and whether inquiries that mention an AI answer already reach you. If two of the three hold, the channel is worth working now.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-geo-worth-it-for-a-small-business/
Sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### Can you text a new lead or a past customer, and what consent do you need?

Text a new lead or a past customer only with the person's consent, and stop as soon as they ask. The FCC's position is that its consent rules cover texts sent with an autodialer, that a reply such as "stop" takes consent back, and that opt-outs must be honored within a reasonable time, no later than ten business days. Answering what someone asked about is different from sending offers, so ask separately before any marketing. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-text-a-new-lead/
Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-24A1.pdf ; https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-67A1.pdf

### Who should own your business phone number?

Your business should own its main phone number, on an account in the business's name, with a login and passcode the owner controls. A personal cell, an employee's line or a number rented from a vendor can leave the business unable to keep or move it. Under the FCC's number porting rules, customers can generally keep a number when they switch providers, and starting a move takes details from the current account. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-should-own-your-business-phone-number/
Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-23-95A1.pdf

### Do you need consent to record calls with customers?

Often, yes. Federal law generally allows a recording when one person on the call agrees, and that person can be you. Florida requires everyone on the call to agree, and some other states may too. Because a caller may be in a stricter state, the safe habit is to tell callers at the start that the call may be recorded, ask whether that is okay, and stop recording if they say no. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-you-need-consent-to-record-customer-calls/
Sources: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/2511 ; http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0900-0999/0934/Sections/0934.03.html

### How do you know how many leads come from your Google Business Profile?

Google's profile performance report shows activity, not leads: how often people clicked the call button, started message conversations, asked for directions or clicked through to your website. A click count cannot tell you who called, whether anyone answered or whether the job was won. To count real leads, log every call and message that came from the profile in your lead tracker, with the source and an outcome.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-count-leads-from-your-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/9918094?hl=en

### How do you cut no-shows for estimates and appointments?

No-shows can often be cut with a few habits: confirm every appointment in writing when it is booked, send a reminder the day before (by text only with the person's consent), make rescheduling a one-step reply, and state a simple, friendly policy. Then record each no-show with the lead's source, so you can see whether some channels bring people who book and do not turn up.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-cut-no-shows/

### Why does ChatGPT recommend my competitor and not me?

Usually because the assistant found it easier to say what your competitor does, where and for whom. No outsider can see exactly why one business is named over another, but the differences an owner can see tend to be plain ones: a clearer description of the work, more recent reviews, more mentions on other sites, or the exact service the customer asked about named in so many words. Which of those weighs, no outsider knows.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-does-chatgpt-recommend-my-competitor/
Sources: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features

### How long does it take to show up in AI answers?

Usually months rather than weeks, and no one can give you a date. Timing depends on the assistant: one that searches the web while it answers can reflect changes once it finds them, while an answer drawn from what a model learned earlier may not change until a newer model is released. Early progress tends to be small: a more accurate description first, then an occasional mention, before inquiries follow.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-long-does-it-take-to-show-up-in-ai-answers/
Sources: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features

### How do you know if a customer found you through ChatGPT?

Usually the only reliable way is to ask. Many people who hear about a business from ChatGPT or another assistant never click a link: they read the name, then search for it, type the web address or call. Those visits tend to look like direct visits or ordinary searches. Ask every new inquiry how they found you, write the answer down next to the lead, and AI answers become a channel you can count.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-tell-if-a-customer-found-you-through-chatgpt/
Sources: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features

### Why does a competitor show up above my business on Google Maps?

Google says local results depend mainly on three things: relevance (how well a profile fits the search), distance (how far the business is from the person searching) and prominence (how well known the business is). A competitor can sit above you because it is closer to that searcher, fits the words they typed better, or is better known, reviews included. Google also says no one can request or pay for a better local ranking.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-does-a-competitor-show-up-above-you-on-google-maps/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177

### Can you get a fake or unfair Google review taken down?

Sometimes. Google says only reviews that break its policies are eligible for removal: for example, a review not based on a real experience, spam, harassment, an off-topic rant or one written from a conflict of interest. An owner can report it from the Business Profile and, if Google finds no violation, appeal once. An honest bad review usually stays. The FTC also says its review rule bars intimidation, groundless legal threats and knowingly false accusations used to stop or remove reviews. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-get-a-fake-google-review-removed/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/4596773 ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114 ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

### Why was my Google Business Profile suspended, and how do I get it back?

Google says it may suspend or disable a Business Profile that does not follow its guidelines, which bar, for example, extra words in the business name, an address the business does not really operate from, and more than one profile per location. To get it back, fix what broke the rules, then file an appeal in Google's appeals tool, optionally with documents such as a business license or utility bill. Google says appeals can be submitted only once, and not to create a new profile.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-was-my-google-business-profile-suspended/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/4569145 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177

### What does it mean when an agency says it is a Google Partner?

Google gives the Partner badge to agencies and other companies that manage Google Ads accounts for other businesses and meet its requirements. Those requirements concern Google Ads: an optimization score, ad spend and Google Ads certifications. So when an agency says it is a Google Partner, that speaks to paid-ads skills and activity. By itself it does not show that the agency can improve free search rankings, map listings or AI answers.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-does-google-partner-mean/
Sources: https://business.google.com/us/support/become-a-partner/ ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9702452 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11410677

### Should you hire an SEO agency that also works for your competitors?

It is not always a problem, but ask before you sign. Agencies often serve several businesses in one field, and an agency working for two rivals can have divided loyalties. Ask whether it has competing clients in your service and area, whether the contract limits that, who sees your lead data, and what happens if a competitor signs later. Get the answers in writing.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-your-seo-agency-work-for-your-competitors/

### What if someone else controls my business’s Google profile?

If someone else owns your verified Google Business Profile, you can ask Google to send an ownership request to the current owner, who has 3 days to respond. If they approve, you can manage the profile. If they refuse, you can appeal. If they do not answer, you may be offered the option to claim it, though Google says that option is not always available.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-if-someone-else-controls-your-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/4566671 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3403100 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/13763036 ; https://support.google.com/business/contact/gmb_3p_complaints ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/12756178

### How do you report a fake business listing on Google Maps?

Google lets you report a business listing even if it is not yours. In Google Maps, open the listing, choose Suggest an edit, then Place is closed or not here, and pick the option that fits, such as “Doesn’t exist here”. For a misleading name, phone number or website that looks fraudulent, Google has a Business Redressal Complaint form, though it says it cannot promise to act on a complaint.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-report-a-fake-business-on-google-maps/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/16043467 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/16109801 ; https://support.google.com/business/contact/business_redressal_form ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/13763036 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177

### What is Microsoft Copilot, and do customers use it to find businesses?

Microsoft describes Copilot as an AI-powered assistant that helps with work: creating content, finding information, summarizing documents, emails and meetings, and analyzing data. Microsoft says it works inside Microsoft 365 apps such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, and in a Copilot mobile app. In Pew Research Center’s February 2026 survey, 17% of U.S. adults said they ever use it, behind ChatGPT and Gemini.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-microsoft-copilot/
Sources: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/solutions/individuals ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### Who should handle new leads when more than one person shares the work?

Give every new lead one named owner, picked by a simple rule written down in advance, and record the name where the whole team can see it. Name a backup for each person's days off, and have the owner leave a short handoff note whenever a lead changes hands. One owner and one note make it much less likely that anyone double-calls a lead or assumes someone else has it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-should-handle-new-leads-on-a-small-team/

### Do you need a logo before you build a website?

No. A website can launch without a logo. At the start it needs a clear business name spelled the same way on the site, in emails and on invoices, one or two colors, and real photos of you and your work. Until a logo is ready, the business name set in plain text does the job. A logo is worth doing once you have a reason to put it somewhere, such as a vehicle or a sign.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-you-need-a-logo-before-a-website/

### Should a service business use video on its website?

Yes, when it shows something text and photos cannot: the owner, the team at work or how a job goes. Keep it short, let visitors choose to press play, add captions to any speech, and keep the key facts in writing too. Video files are usually much heavier than photos, so check that your pages still load quickly on a phone before you add one.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-use-video-on-your-website/
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/video-usability/ ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/media/av/captions/ ; https://web.dev/learn/performance/video-performance

### Should a small business website use pop-ups?

Usually not, at least not one that appears as soon as a visitor lands. Nielsen Norman Group says decades of its user research show that people dislike pop-ups, which tend to appear at the wrong time and interrupt people during critical tasks. For a service visitor, that task is often a call or an inquiry. A visible phone number, an on-page form and a small, dismissible banner are gentler ways to ask.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-your-website-use-pop-ups/
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/popups/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/avoid-intrusive-interstitials

### Is pay-for-performance SEO a good deal?

Often not, when payment depends only on ranking. The agency is then paid for reaching a position, so the easiest searches are the natural choice, and those are often ones that bring no customers. A better deal ties payment to inquiries you can trace to a source, or to jobs won, with the rules for what counts agreed in writing before work starts.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-pay-for-performance-seo-a-good-deal/

### What should you say when a customer repeats something wrong an AI told them?

Stay calm, thank the customer for checking, and say what is actually true in plain words. Do not argue with the assistant or make the customer feel foolish. Offer to confirm the correct detail in writing, and note what you heard. If the wrong detail came from your own website or profile, fix it there, because that is the part you control.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/when-a-customer-repeats-something-wrong-an-ai-told-them/

### What is Claude, and do customers use it to find businesses?

Anthropic describes Claude as “a helpful, intuitive, and powerful collaborator” you can put to work on real tasks. Anthropic lists searching the web for current information among Claude’s tools, and says Claude runs on the web, on phones and in a desktop app. In Pew Research Center’s February 2026 survey, 6% of U.S. adults said they ever use it, well behind ChatGPT at 44%.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-claude/
Sources: https://claude.com/product/overview ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### What is Meta AI, and can it recommend businesses to customers?

Meta AI is the assistant Meta builds into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, and also offers on a website and in its own app. Meta announced it in September 2023. Its later posts suggest asking it for recommendations, including for a restaurant, and say it can search the web. In Pew Research Center’s February 2026 survey, 14% of U.S. adults said they ever use it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-meta-ai/
Sources: https://about.fb.com/news/2023/09/introducing-ai-powered-assistants-characters-and-creative-tools/ ; https://about.fb.com/news/2024/04/meta-ai-assistant-built-with-llama-3/ ; https://about.fb.com/news/2025/04/introducing-meta-ai-app-new-way-access-ai-assistant/ ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### Do Siri and Alexa recommend local businesses?

Siri can find nearby places and Alexa+ can book some services, but no one can promise either will name a particular business. Apple says that with Location Services on, Siri can find places nearby, and that Siri can use ChatGPT once a person sets it up. Amazon says Alexa+ can make reservations or appointments with OpenTable and Vagaro, and can suggest a restaurant.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-siri-and-alexa-recommend-local-businesses/
Sources: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/turn-on-chatgpt-iph00fd3c8c2/ios ; https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/use-siri-to-get-answers-from-chatgpt-iph0193a9d54/27/ios/27 ; https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/find-info-and-get-things-done-ipha48873ed6/27/ios/27 ; https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/devices/new-alexa-generative-artificial-intelligence ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/

### Why does ChatGPT give different people different answers?

ChatGPT answers can differ from person to person because it does not work from one fixed script. OpenAI says it can use a person’s memory, an approximate location taken from their IP address, and a web search it may run when a question would benefit from current information. Two people asking the same question can get different answers, so one check from your own account shows what your account sees, not necessarily what a customer sees.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-does-chatgpt-give-different-people-different-answers/
Sources: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt ; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features

### Who should own your Google Ads and Facebook ad accounts?

The business should own its Google Ads and Facebook ad accounts: set up under a login the owner controls, billed to the business, with at least two administrators from the business at all times. An agency can work in the account at a lower access level, such as Standard in Google Ads or Advertiser at Meta, instead of sharing a password, and the owner can end that access when the work ends.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-should-own-your-ad-accounts/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9978556 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/155909647811305 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1143109949216644

### What answer options should 'How did you hear about us?' have?

Give customers a short list of plain-language options and sort each one into a lead channel: search, AI answer, social, referral, paid, email, campaign or direct. Split 'Google' into search results, the map listing, an AI answer and an ad, since people often use one word for all four. Add an 'Other' box, make the form version optional, and always ask out loud on calls.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-did-you-hear-about-us-options/

### What should you ask before hiring a web designer?

Before hiring a web designer, ask who will own the domain, the design and the logins; who writes the words and supplies the photos; how the site looks and loads on a phone; where inquiries go and how you will know they arrive; and what happens after launch. Then open sites the designer built on your own phone and judge them by how they work, not only by how they look.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/questions-to-ask-before-hiring-a-web-designer/

### Why do my business calls show up as 'Spam Likely' on customers' phones?

Labels such as 'Spam Likely' come from call-labeling services, which the FCC says some phone companies offer. The FCC also says legitimate callers can be blocked by mistake when their calls resemble unwanted ones. An owner can help by calling only with the person's consent, from a valid number that is really theirs, keeping calls per minute and repeat call-backs low, and leaving a voicemail with one consistent call-back number. The owner cannot control what a customer's carrier or phone shows.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-do-your-business-calls-show-as-spam/
Sources: https://www.fcc.gov/call-blocking ; https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication

### What does 'direct' traffic mean in your website analytics?

In Google Analytics, direct traffic is the channel for visits that arrive by a saved link or by someone entering your address. Visits can land there for other reasons too, such as a link opened from some apps or email programs, or a customer who heard your name from a person or an AI answer and then typed it. It counts visits, not who became a customer, so your lead records tell you more.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-direct-traffic/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9756891

### Google Ads or Facebook ads: which is better for a service business?

Neither is better for every service business, because they reach people at different moments. Google Ads can put your business in front of someone who is searching for the service right now, which often suits urgent jobs. Facebook ads usually reach people who are scrolling and were not looking, which can suit work that sells on looks and trust. Judge both by jobs won, not by clicks.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/google-ads-or-facebook-ads/
Sources: https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/ ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722080 ; https://www.facebook.com/help/562973647153813

### Are you paying for fake or accidental clicks on your Google Ads?

Google defines invalid clicks as clicks that do not show genuine interest in your business, such as accidental clicks, bots and manual clicks that increase your costs. It says it filters them out of your billing, and gives a credit where appropriate and possible when it finds some later. If you suspect traffic it missed, you can ask Google to investigate the last 60 days. Your own count of calls and jobs is usually the better check.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-you-paying-for-fake-ad-clicks/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/42995 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11182074

### How should you answer the phone when a new customer calls?

Answer with the business name, your own name and an offer to help. Capture a name and number first, then three things: what the caller needs, where the job is and when they want it. Ask how they heard about you, agree one clear next step with a time, and send a confirmation text only with the person's consent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-answer-the-phone-for-a-new-customer/

### What is the difference between a domain, hosting and a website, and how do you find out who hosts yours?

A domain is your web address, hosting is the rented computer space where your site's files are kept, and the website is the pages, words and photos visitors see. A business site usually involves all three, and the business should control each account. To find who hosts yours, check billing records, ask whoever built the site and look at where your domain points. A domain lookup shows registration data, which may not name the host.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/domain-hosting-and-website-difference/
Sources: https://lookup.icann.org/

### What happens if your business domain name expires?

Under ICANN's Expired Registration Recovery Policy, registrars must send at least two reminders before a covered domain name expires and at least one more after it if the name is not renewed or deleted. After expiry the name can stop pointing to your website and email, a registrar may delete it at any time after expiry, subject to other ICANN rules, and a 30-day redemption period can follow deletion. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-happens-if-your-domain-expires/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/consensus-policies/expired-registration-recovery-policy/expired-registration-recovery-policy-21-02-2024-en ; https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/consensus-policies/expired-registration-recovery-policy/expired-registration-recovery-policy-28-02-2013-en

## Questions and answers

### What does Ascent Vision do?

Ascent Vision is a Florida marketing company. It makes service businesses visible on Google and in AI answers, builds the lead systems that turn those visits into inquiries, and upgrades or builds the website they run on. Every lead is tracked back to where it came from.

### Is Ascent Vision the same company as Ascent Vision Technologies or CACI Ascent Vision?

No. Ascent Vision LLC is a Florida marketing company founded in 2026 by Clayton Camera and Grayson Sorrentino. CACI Ascent Vision, LLC (formerly Ascent Vision Technologies) is a Montana imaging and counter-drone company, owned by CACI International since 2020, that does business as "Ascent Vision" in federal contracting records. The two have never been connected.

### What is GEO?

GEO, generative engine optimization, is the work of making a business the one AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers recommend when a customer asks them who to call. People now ask assistants as well as search engines, so being part of that answer matters alongside ranking.

### How is GEO different from SEO?

SEO aims for a ranked link on a search results page. GEO aims for a mention or recommendation inside an AI-written answer. The two support each other, and Ascent Vision measures them separately, because a business that ranks is not always the business an assistant recommends.

### How do I know what the work produced?

Every lead from an Ascent Vision site or campaign is recorded with where it came from, such as a search, an AI answer, a referral or an ad, so a client can see which leads the work produced and what happened to each one.

### Do you publish prices?

No. Every engagement is scoped on a call first, because the work depends on the business, the market and what already exists. Start with the application on the Work with us page: nine short questions, about two minutes.

### Can I meet Ascent Vision in person?

Yes. Most of Ascent Vision's meetings are by video call, and clients near Tallahassee, Florida, can also meet the founders in person by appointment.

### Who does Ascent Vision work with?

Ascent Vision works with small businesses and independent professionals who sell a service and want more of their customers to find them through search and AI answers. Its first client is an online fitness coaching business.

### Who owns the website and the content?

The client owns their domain, their content and their lead data. Ascent Vision builds and runs the work; it does not hold a client's site or customers hostage.
